title: How many SKY130 mappings does a generic-gate screen need to find the best area × latency design?
summary: Using the 40 SKY130-mapped MAC-engine designs of eda-sky130rung as ground truth (Yosys 0.33, ABC dc2; map, SKY130 HD tt 25 °C 1.80 V), three cheap screens rank the designs and only the top k get the expensive mapping. The best design (p = 4 lanes, 4 bits) is first in the generic cells × cycles order for area × cycles, area × latency and latency alike, and fifth for the free analytic model. Over 5,000 random pools of 20 designs, mapping 3 captures the pool's best 0.970 of the time (Wilson 95% 0.965–0.975) against 0.15 for random choice, and 0.987 when logic depth is added, even though depth ranks the mapped delay at only Spearman 0.611. One mapping already lands within 1.078× of the pool optimum on average. Preliminary: one design family, 40 points (the intervals cover only the random draws, not family variation), a synthesis-model truth with no place and route, and counts of mappings rather than seconds. No input is invented: all numbers come from the committed mapped data.
lede: a generic-gate cells × cycles screen puts the best SKY130 area × latency design first among 40 MAC engines; over random pools of 20, mapping 3 designs finds the pool's best 97% of the time, against 15% for random choice.
